document_title: Aurora's driverless trucks at the scale, and the letter's own numbers
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Aurora told its shareholders about weigh stations.

Autonomous trucks have relied on voluntary inspections to bypass them, the October 28th letter says. It says the Aurora Driver can now tell whether a station is open, steer to an available scale lane and adapt to different scale configurations.

The letter puts the production ramp about six weeks behind its prior plan. Third quarter revenue was $3 million against a $257 million operating loss, stock-based compensation included.

Aurora names Dallas to Houston as its own route. Charger Logistics plans to start between Dallas and Laredo under a non-binding MOU, the letter says.

The letter is on the SEC's EDGAR site. Has a Texas scale house weighed a driverless Aurora truck yet?

#AuroraInnovation #Houston #Laredo

S1.headline: The truck can now tell if the scale is open
S1.body: Aurora says its driverless trucks can now tell whether a weigh station is open and steer to an available scale lane on their own.
strings: The truck can now tell if the scale is open
Aurora says its driverless trucks can now tell whether a weigh station is open and steer to an available scale lane on their own.

S2.headline: Open, which lane, which scale
S2.body: Autonomous trucks have relied on voluntary inspections to bypass weigh stations, the letter says. It says the Aurora Driver can now handle three steps on its own.
strings: Autonomous trucks have relied on voluntary inspections to bypass weigh stations, the letter says. It says the Aurora Driver can now handle three steps on its own.

S3.headline: Next, through the security gate
S3.body: Aurora says that in November its trucks will drive directly to sites for several customers, through security checkpoints.
strings: Aurora says that in November its trucks will drive directly to sites for several customers, through security checkpoints.

S4.headline: 20+ driverless trucks are built
S4.body: The letter says production is accelerating. The Aurora Driver passed 500,000 commercial driverless miles in September with 100% on-time delivery since launch, by Aurora's own count.
strings: The letter says production is accelerating. The Aurora Driver passed 500,000 commercial driverless miles in September with 100% on-time delivery since launch, by Aurora's own count.

S5.headline: About six weeks behind its own plan
S5.body: Material availability, component quality and problems found in end-of-line testing held the ramp back, the letter says. Aurora now expects 20 trucks a week in early December.
strings: About six weeks behind its own plan
Material availability, component quality and problems found in end-of-line testing held the ramp back, the letter says. Aurora now expects 20 trucks a week in early December.

S6.headline: $3 million in revenue, a $257 million operating loss
S6.body: Third quarter revenue and operating loss at one scale. The loss includes stock-based compensation. Aurora expects about $9 million of revenue for 2026.
strings: $3 million in revenue, a $257 million operating loss
Third quarter revenue and operating loss at one scale. The loss includes stock-based compensation. Aurora expects about $9 million of revenue for 2026.

S7.headline: Aurora's own route, and a customer's plan
S7.body: Dallas to Houston is Aurora's own route. Charger Logistics plans to start between Dallas and Laredo under a non-binding MOU for 500 trucks, with delivery expected in 2027 and 2028. Routes drawn straight between places. New Braunfels is marked at Comal County's center.
strings: Aurora's own route, and a customer's plan

Dallas to Houston is Aurora's own route. Charger Logistics plans to start between Dallas and Laredo under a non-binding MOU for 500 trucks, with delivery expected in 2027 and 2028. Routes drawn straight between places. New Braunfels is marked at Comal County's center.

S8.headline: When it stops, a light on the cab
S8.body: The letter says FMCSA granted a five-year exemption letting driverless trucks use cab-mounted warning beacons in place of warning devices set out by hand.
strings: When it stops, a light on the cab
The letter says FMCSA granted a five-year exemption letting driverless trucks use cab-mounted warning beacons in place of warning devices set out by hand.

S9.headline: From 20+ built to 1,000+ expected
S9.body: Aurora expects more than 200 trucks by the end of February and more than 1,000 in operation at the end of 2027. Each primer stall is one expected truck. The filing is on the SEC's EDGAR site, dated October 28th.
